body: B BarMatrix Home The Method Drills Pricing SIGN IN START THE FREE DIAGNOSTIC ← ALL DRILLS CQ14141 SUBJECT Civil Procedure SUBTOPIC Motions DIFFICULTY ▮▮▮▮▮ Dovesound Review BARMATRIX Q#14141_dovesound_review Lydia Sound Systems, a company that sells portable speakers for Christian conferences and Bible-study events, filed suit in federal district court against Mary, a reporter for The Berean Review, a consumer-product testing website. The suit arose after Mary published a review of Lydia Sound Systems’ “DoveSound” speakers. The court ruled that Lydia Sound Systems was a “public figure” and thus had to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Mary made a false and disparaging statement about the speakers with “actual malice.” “Actual malice” requires knowledge that one is making a false statement or reckless disregard of the truthfulness of one’s statement. Mary moved for summary judgm

buttons.text: AYes, because Lydia Sound Systems did not meet its burden to defeat Mary’s motion for summary judgme
BYes, because Lydia Sound Systems acted in bad faith by not providing evidence to contradict Mary’s
CNo, because a party to a suit may not submit a personal affidavit as evidence in support of her own
DNo, because the court should first order Lydia Sound Systems to respond to Mary’s motion for summar
